expected_output.reasoning:
The agent correctly cites AWS's "up to 60% less energy" figure attributed to AWS, correctly flags SQL Server as having no Graviton option, and recommends PostgreSQL instance class change and Lambda arm64 switch as straightforward. However, it fails several specific required elements: (1) it does not give a percentage emissions saving for the fleet is partially avoided but the agent still implies the fleet-wide savings will be "below 60%" and applies the 60% figure as an estimate to most of the fleet ("expect savings in the neighborhood of that ~60% energy/CO2 figure"), which is exactly what the expected output says NOT to do - it explicitly states the 60% figure should not be applied to the customer's fleet. (2) It completely omits the required explanation that the effect on reported emissions cannot be predicted due to the methodology pooling EC2 emissions in a cluster and allocating by normalized instance-hours, and does not express impact as vCPU-hours moved to Graviton tracked through compute intensity. (3) It does not mention m5 as a previous-generation family. (4) It does not explicitly recommend using Compute Optimizer migration effort or the transition guide for the EC2 fleet compatibility check (it only generically says "check for x86-only binaries"). These are substantial gaps against the detailed expected methodology, so the response does not meet the expected criteria despite covering some surface-level points correctly.</reasoning>
<parameter name="evidence">"For everything except the SQL Server instance, expect savings in the neighborhood of that **~60%** energy/CO2 figure, assuming sizing and utilization stay sensible post-migration." and no mention of normalized instance-hours, vCPU-hours, compute intensity, or m5 being previous-generation.
